critique: The large, unmistakably hairless guinea pig—with rose-taupe skin, charcoal-and-rust face, glossy eyes, floppy ears, pink nose, and white whiskers—commands the vertical frame, and the fine watercolor-like vegetation convincingly echoes Dürer’s patient naturalism. However, the wide-eyed expression and mouthful of many blades miss the specified half-closed, corner-of-mouth delight, while the generic meadow lacks the original’s clearly cut clod, exposed roots, dark soil, and distinct dandelion flower and seed head.
